title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Rule on Weekly Payability, Charging and Payment Issue
content:
**(a) Conditions of a weekly payment.** On an Unemployment Benefit Claims record a weekly payment is issued for a certified week only when all of the following hold:

1. the certification is timely or late with good cause;
2. the claimant answered able and available with no refused work;
3. the required work-search contacts were reported or waived;
4. the week is not a waiting week; and
5. no hold is in force.

**(b) Claim status.** A weekly payment may be issued only while the claim status is active.

**(c) One payment per week and kind.** A payment may be issued only once per claim per week ending date and payment kind, so a week already paid is corrected only by a supplemental payment and a cancelled payment is replaced only by a reissue.

**(d) Retired clauses.** The following clauses are no longer in force and are superseded by the current basis:

- "A week in which hours worked reach the full-time hours threshold is not a week of unemployment and nothing is paid."
- "Otherwise the earnings deduction is the part of gross earnings above the earnings disregard, which is the disregard share of the weekly benefit amount."
- "The other-pay deduction is vacation and holiday pay allocated to the week where deductible, plus the weekly-prorated base-period-employer pension times the pension offset share, using the claimant-contributed share where the claimant paid into the plan; severance pay is not deducted."
- "The payable amount is the weekly benefit amount plus dependency allowance minus both deductions, rounded down to the whole dollar, never below zero and never more than the remaining benefit balance; a payable amount of zero records no payment."

**(e) Exhaustion.** When the payment brings the remaining benefit balance to zero the claim is exhausted.

**(f) Method.** The payment is issued through the payment method in force on the payment date.

**(g) Charge code.** Each payment carries the charge code of its program:

| Program's employer charge share | Charge code carried by the payment |
|---|---|
| One | State chargeable |
| One half | Extended Benefits shared |
| Zero | Non-charged |

**(h) Offsets and withholding.** Overpayment offsets and withholding deductions are taken from the payable amount after it is computed and do not change the amount charged to the balance.

## Points of judgement

- The status and hold read under (a)5 and (b) are those on the claim records on the payment date.
- Under (c), a second weekly payment, or a second reissue, for the same claim and week ending date is barred; a supplemental entry is the form a correction takes.
- Under (h), a hypothetical payable amount of 300.00 from which a 50.00 overpayment offset is taken is still charged to the balance at 300.00.

superseded_clauses: Otherwise the earnings deduction is the part of gross earnings above the earnings disregard, which is the disregard share of the weekly benefit amount.
A week in which hours worked reach the full-time hours threshold is not a week of unemployment and nothing is paid.

The other-pay deduction is vacation and holiday pay allocated to the week where deductible, plus the weekly-prorated base-period-employer pension times the pension offset share, using the claimant-contributed share where the claimant paid into the plan; severance pay is not deducted.

The payable amount is the weekly benefit amount plus dependency allowance minus both deductions, rounded down to the whole dollar, never below zero and never more than the remaining benefit balance; a payable amount of zero records no payment.
